rationale: Dispatches the measurement that answers why the origin's decided index never advances, after a local run that also corrects the wording of my last counterevidence. The case now reports what the origin itself believes at the sample point, and locally it reports `origin_promise_pid` 3 with `origin_phase_accept` true while its decided index is still 0. So the origin was re-prepared and re-synchronised by the new leader - its promise moved and it entered the accept phase, which only happens through an `AcceptSync` - and its decided index stayed 0 because that `AcceptSync` carried decided index 0, i.e. the new leader itself had decided nothing (the same run reports its own entry 22 unresolved). That contradicts the sentence I recorded last turn, that this scenario does not exercise a completed re-synchronisation at all: it does exercise it, and the re-synchronisation simply carries no decided progress. The shift still appears with the origin at index 4 while entry 33 sits at index 2, so the defect account is unchanged; what changes is the explanation of the phase field, which is now measured rather than inferred.

investigations.discriminator: Pending the submitted case's receipt. Locally the origin's promise points at the new leader and its phase is Accept while its decided index is 0, so the re-synchronisation does happen and carries no decided progress; what remains open is why the new leader never decides its own entry in this construction, which is what would let the receipts exercise a re-synchronisation that both completes and carries progress.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds two measurements to every case's outcome event - the origin's promise pid and whether its phase is Accept at the point where the re-synchronisation is sampled - so the receipts say whether the origin was re-prepared or never processed a prepare, rather than leaving that to inference. The scenario, the poll flag, the tick periods and the comparisons are unchanged; a fresh execution is required because the harness bytes changed.

scope.description: One run of the separation case: the lost-entry scenario at a 1000 ms tick period where the harness polls the origin's decided index for up to thirty seconds before re-electing it, and additionally records the origin's promise pid and accept-phase flag at that sample so a re-synchronisation that happened can be told apart from one that never started. The run then re-elects the origin, buffers a fresh entry with two filler appends, and reports the returned index against the entry's true position as before.
assumptions: The origin's promise pid moving to another node, together with its phase being Accept, is evidence that it processed a prepare and an accept-sync from that node, because the phase only becomes Accept through `handle_acceptsync`.
Everything else in the case is unchanged from the previous revision, so any difference in the outcome is attributable to the added measurements.
No target logic is modified; the harness only reads the origin's own reported state.
excluded: Any claim about why the new leader does not decide its own entry; only what the origin reports is observed here.
Any claim about the internal placeholder queue, which is not reachable through the public API.
Any claim about tick periods other than 1000 ms in this case.

experiment.prefix: Build three actors with batch_size 3 and a 1000 ms tick period, node 1 carrying leader_priority 1. Elect node 1, emit the admission event, buffer `append_notify(11)` and `append_notify(12)` on it, block its links to nodes 2 and 3, let node 3 take over and accept entry 22, then unblock and poll node 1's decided index every 500 ms for up to thirty seconds. At that point record node 1's promise pid and accept-phase flag as well as its decided index, then call `try_become_leader()` on it until it reports itself as the accepted leader, spawn `append_notify(33)`, follow with plain appends 34 and 35, sleep, and await the fresh call. Read node 1's decided suffix, find the true position of entry 33, read the entry at the returned index, and emit the outcome event with the resolution, both indices, whether they agree, the entry at the returned index, the decided values, the poll wait, the completion flag, the origin's promise pid and its accept-phase flag.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: the origin's promise and phase are its own reported state, batching defers the writes into `unconfirmed_local`, and `reconcile_unconfirmed` maps queued placeholders to index advances to compute the index it reports. The harness chooses the schedule and reads the endpoints.

comparisons.description: If the fresh call resolves Ok, the returned index must be the entry's true position; locally violated again, so a violation is expected.

semantic_changes: Two read-only measurements added to the outcome event (the origin's promise pid and accept-phase flag at the re-synchronisation sample); no scenario or comparison change.
